title: Auth sign-up (centered card)
summary: Production-grade sign-up page composing the auth-sign-up-card block. Email + password (with confirm) + optional name + terms checkbox + optional social providers, all routed through a pluggable AuthAdapter.
brief: Ship a sign-up page wired to my auth library — name (optional) + email + password + confirm password + terms checkbox, with optional GitHub/Google social buttons and a destructive Alert error surface.

steps.reason: The page-level block — wires the form state, social handoff, error display, and pending state. Routes account creation through the supplied AuthAdapter.
Field a11y wiring (FormItem / FormControl) when consumers extend with RHF
Submit + social CTAs (loading prop drives the busy state)
Inline error surface for failed sign-up
Visual divider between social and credential sections

checklist.check: Pass an AuthAdapter via the `adapter` prop with `signUpWithPassword` implemented. The block surfaces an 'unimplemented' error if the user submits without it.
Provide an `onSuccess` handler that navigates the user (typically to /verify-email after sign-up). The block does not navigate by itself.
Keep `passwordMinLength` aligned with the auth-reset-password block so users don't hit a stricter rule on reset than they did at signup.
Set `termsHref` and `privacyHref` to your real legal pages. The defaults (/terms, /privacy) are placeholders and will 404 until you add the routes.
Adapter methods must return `{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }` on failure (never throw). The block reads `error.message` into the Alert.
[AuthSignUpCard] Avoid: Forgetting to pass the AuthAdapter — the block has no built-in fallback and surfaces an 'unimplemented' error on submit.
[AuthSignUpCard] Avoid: Skipping onSuccess and relying on adapter.redirect alone — the redirect is informational; the consumer's onSuccess handler is what actually navigates.

[AuthSignUpCard] Avoid: Wiring auth state inside the adapter methods instead of returning { ok, error } — the block reads result.error.message into the Alert; throwing inside the adapter loses the structured payload.
[AuthSignUpCard] Avoid: Setting termsHref / privacyHref to absolute URLs when in-app routes exist — they're plain anchor hrefs; prefer relative paths so the consumer's router handles navigation.

[AuthSignUpCard] Avoid: Forgetting that name is optional — passing required={true} on the name field would lock out users who don't want to share it; the block already treats name as optional and trims whitespace before forwarding.

[AuthSignUpCard] A11y: All inputs have explicit Label htmlFor pairing, autoComplete='email' / 'new-password', and required attributes where relevant. The password helper text is wired via aria-describedby. Submit button uses the canonical loading prop (sets aria-busy + disabled). Errors render in an Alert with role='alert' so they're announced. Terms checkbox label is clickable and the legal links remain reachable by keyboard.
[Card] Avoid: Nesting cards
[Card] Avoid: Using Card when a simple div with border would suffice
[Card] Avoid: Forgetting CardContent padding when placing forms inside
[Card] A11y: Card is a div by default. Add role='region' and aria-labelledby (pointing to CardTitle's id) for landmark cards. CardTitle renders h3 — ensure heading hierarchy is correct on the page.
[Form] Avoid: Forgetting to spread {...field} into the form control (connects value/onChange)
[Form] Avoid: Putting FormLabel outside FormItem (loses htmlFor wiring)
[Form] Avoid: Using useForm without a resolver when zod validation is desired
[Form] Avoid: Calling form.handleSubmit without a callback

[Form] A11y: FormControl automatically wires id, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid. FormLabel uses htmlFor matching the control id. Errors are announced via FormMessage with matching aria-describedby.
[Label] Avoid: Forgetting to set htmlFor matching the input's id
[Label] Avoid: Using Label for non-form text content
[Label] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside Label
[Label] A11y: Clicking the label focuses the associated control. Automatically communicates the label to screen readers. Use htmlFor/id pairing, not nesting.
[Input] Avoid: Missing associated Label element for accessibility
[Input] Avoid: Using type='number' without min/max constraints
[Input] Avoid: Not providing placeholder text for context
[Input] A11y: Always pair with a Label using htmlFor/id. Consider aria-describedby for helper text or error messages.
[Checkbox] Avoid: Missing Label pairing
[Checkbox] Avoid: Using onChange instead of onCheckedChange
[Checkbox] Avoid: Forgetting that onCheckedChange can receive 'indeterminate' as well as boolean
[Checkbox] A11y: Always pair with Label via htmlFor/id. Radix handles aria-checked automatically.
[Button] Avoid: Nesting interactive elements inside asChild button
[Button] Avoid: Using — breaks middle-click, cmd-click, and right-click → 'open in new tab', and skips the browser history entry
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button variant='destructive'> for recoverable actions like 'Reset filters' — reserve destructive for delete/archive/leave; use 'secondary' or 'ghost' for resets
[Button] Avoid: Using <Button size='icon'> without an aria-label — screen readers have nothing to announce; always pair icon-only buttons with aria-label or visible text
[Button] A11y: Automatically handles focus ring, disabled state, and aria attributes. Icon-only buttons MUST have aria-label. Loading state automatically sets disabled.
[Alert] Avoid: Using destructive for non-error messages
[Alert] Avoid: Missing AlertTitle (reduces scannability)
[Alert] Avoid: Stacking multiple Alerts on the same page instead of grouping
[Alert] A11y: Root renders role='alert' so screen readers announce it. For non-urgent info banners consider role='status' or aria-live='polite' via className overrides.
[Separator] Avoid: Using as spacing instead of semantic separation
[Separator] Avoid: Forgetting orientation='vertical' needs parent height
[Separator] A11y: Set decorative=false if the separator conveys semantic meaning. Radix handles role='separator'.
